title: Understanding MAE
text: The Mean Absolute Error (MAE) is a measure of errors between paired observations expressing the same phenomenon. It is calculated as the average of the absolute differences between predicted values and observed values.

title: Effect of Shuffling Data
text: Consider what happens to the mean of a dataset when you shuffle the data. Does the mean change? How does this relate to the MAE?

title: Shuffling and Mean
text: If you shuffle the order of the rows in a dataset, does the mean of the dataset change?

title: MAE and Constant Model
text: In a constant model where the prediction is always the same value, think about how the MAE is calculated. What role does the mean of the dataset play in this calculation?

hintAnswer: The mean of the observed values
title: MAE Calculation
text: When using a constant model, what value minimizes the MAE?
choices: The mean of the observed values
The median of the observed values
The mode of the observed values
